ai.description: This large turtle reaches 48 cm. It features a grey-brown carapace with three distinct longitudinal black stripes and a yellow head with a red-orange snout stripe. The plastron is uniformly yellow.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Batagur dhongoka* is best distinguished by the three distinct, longitudinal black stripes running along the length of its otherwise tan or olive-colored carapace.
ai.habitat: The Three-striped Roofed Turtle inhabits deep, flowing rivers and large tributaries of the Ganges and Brahmaputra basins, preferring areas with sandy banks and sparse vegetation.
ai.behavior: The Three-striped Roofed Turtle is primarily diurnal, spending much of its day basking on logs or sandbanks to regulate its body temperature before foraging for aquatic plants.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Batagur dhongoka* is oviparous, nesting from February to April. Females lay a single clutch of 20–30 elliptical eggs in sandy riverbanks across northern India.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Three-striped Roofed Turtle inhabits the Ganges, Chambal, and Brahmaputra river systems across northern and northeastern India, primarily at low to moderate elevations.
